corrections: Brian Painter: the county's page says only that he was elected District 1 Commissioner in November 2010; the 2022 re-election is shown by the official 2022 recap, not by that page, so the office wording now says so.
Jennie Y. Haymond: the unlinked mention of an Attorney General release taken out of the office wording.
Anne Delahanty: the unlinked claim about the 2022 results taken out of the office wording.
Amy Beth Beasley and Matthew Lehman: the website 'how' now describes only what the campaign sites themselves show.
note: The session's shared web-search allowance ran out at this part's first searches, so the rest was read from pages reached directly: county, city and school-district sites and the State Board of Elections' official 2022 general election recaps (elect.ky.gov, one PDF per county). The recaps for Greenup, Powell, Elliott, Scott, Bell, Fulton, Meade, Owen, Clay, Breathitt and Fayette gave no text to the kit's PDF reader, and the Bell, Whitley and Winchester sites did not answer, so those candidates rest on what other pages show. Party pages that list a candidate without endorsing (Campbell County Republicans for Brian Painter, Fayette County Democrats for Amy Beasley) are already in ballot/lean/ky_endorsements.json as support and are not recorded here. Fulton County's constables page names a James Bridges as Constable, District 4, but nothing ties him to the James Bridges running for jailer, so it is left out. Johnny Templin ran for Nicholasville City Commission in 2022 and was not elected (official recap), so no office is recorded.
